title: Are Sinners Now So Senseless Grown
description: Are Sinners Now So Senseless Grown in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 14, part 2, headed “The folly of persecutors”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Are sin-ners now so sense-less grown That they thy saints de-vour? And nev-er wor-ship at thy throne, Nor fear thine aw-ful power?

lines: Are sinners now so senseless grown
And never worship at thy throne,
Great God appear to their surprise,
Let them no more thy wrath despise,
Nor turn our hope to shame.
Dost thou not dwell among the just?
That we should make thy name our trust;
O that the joyful day were come
When God shall bring his children home,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
